data.narrative:
Enigma is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jonathan Jacobi and Gal Niv, both former Unit 8200 members with prior tenures at Microsoft and Check Point. The company has raised $71M to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector includes 9 peer companies—1 public and 8 private—though the narrow peer set at equivalent stage and valuation tier proved insufficient for robust median analysis.

Stage-progression methodology was the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($71M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier yields an implied valuation of $178M. This method rests on the assumption that Enigma's future funding round reflects standard progression multiples for the sector, though actual outcomes depend on operational milestones and market conditions not visible in current data.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $151M (low) to $204M (high), centered at $178M (median). Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently dense peer comparables at identical stage and valuation tier, which limits confidence in the median figure derived from a single method. Additionally, the valuation proxy relies on total raised rather than disclosed post-money valuations, introducing potential distortion if Enigma's capital efficiency differs materially from sector norms. Investors should treat this range as preliminary pending access to more granular comparable transaction data or disclosure of the company's actual post-money from recent rounds.
